articles.title: Problematic or protected? The debate over filming police in real time
articles.summary: Social media posts showing real-time positions of police officers in a standoff with an armed suspect at the University of Toronto's Mississauga campus on Monday night prompted a stern warning from police, but legal experts say the law isn't clear-cut on the issue.

articles.title: Unifor says it thinks Stellantis has sold Brampton assembly plant
articles.summary: A union representing Stellantis autoworkers says it thinks the company has sold its idled assembly plant in southern Ontario.

articles.title: Hitachi Rail opens new Canadian headquarters in Scarborough
articles.summary: Hitachi Rail officially opened its new Canadian headquarters in Scarborough on Friday. The headquarters will be the base for more than 1,100 employees and 100 paid interns a year, it says.

articles.title: Tesla’s Cybertruck heads for an exit after years of hype and division
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Tesla’s Cybertruck, the hulking, stainless-steel pickup that inspired devotion and derision with its science-fiction looks, will cease production next year.

articles.title: Man charged after woman fatally stabbed in North York, police say
articles.summary: A man has been arrested and charged after a woman was fatally stabbed in North York on Friday morning, Toronto police say.

articles.title: City of Toronto pauses hiring, citing 'financial pressures' ahead of budget season
articles.summary: As Toronto stares down another difficult budget season, with a $1-billion shortfall, a hiring freeze is being put in place at city hall. The pause won't apply to emergency services, but means some job applications have been paused partway through the process.

articles.title: U of T dean of dentistry steps down after investigation into antisemitic images in course material
articles.summary: The University of Toronto says its dean of dentistry Anil Kishen voluntarily stepped down following an investigation into his use of antisemitic imagery in February.

articles.title: 2 women, 2 children, struck by vehicle in Richmond Hill, Ont.: police
articles.summary: York Regional Police say four pedestrians, including two children, were struck by a vehicle in Richmond Hill, north of Toronto, on Thursday afternoon.

articles.title: Toronto fire chief welcomes new lithium-ion regulations in record-setting year for battery fires
articles.summary: Toronto's fire chief says new regulations from Queen's Park to ban people from modifying lithium-ion batteries are a welcome "first step." The city has already seen more than 120 blazes sparked by the batteries this year alone.
